edits.old: To ask which of these haplotypes are present in cultivated barley, we compared five European spring malting cultivars released between 2012 and 2018 with the wild haplotype groups at the same four genes (Fig. 3f–i; Online Resource 10). At *GPAT6*, the five cultivars matched the two low-fiber haplotype groups at 95–98% and 88–91% of called sites but the high-fiber group at only 39–45%, so the high-fiber wild haplotype is essentially absent from these lines. The cultivars, like the two low-fiber groups, carried the reference (Morex) allele at only 12–14% of these sites, against 65% in the high-fiber group. At *GH17* and *PHT4;3*, by contrast, all five cultivars carried the reference allele at every called site. At the four SNPs that defined the haplotypes of the GDSL esterase/lipase gene, the five cultivars carried the alleles of the low-fiber, high-starch haplotype A at every called site, and none carried those of the high-fiber, low-starch haplotype B (Fig. 3i).
